question_or_proposition: How should footnote *4 be interpreted to determine when the once-per-permit-term Whole Effluent Toxicity test must be performed—specifically, whether its listed conditions (first springtime after the permit effective date, irrigation season, likely irrigation return flows to the Animas River, presence of sensitive juvenile life forms, and colder ambient temperatures affecting treatment) are conjunctive timing prerequisites that must all be satisfied, and whether that interpretation makes WET monitoring required or not required during any part of Federal FY2025?
required_context: WET monitoring rows for Ceriodaphnia dubia and Pimephales promelas (Once/Term, Report value) on page 4
Footnotes *1 (When discharging) and *3 (monitoring begins on permit effective date)
Permit effective date and permit term needed to identify the first springtime after effective date
Outfall 001 intermittent-flow authorization and seasonal discharge context from Section A
notes: The nominated span specifies conditional, seasonal timing for once-per-term WET testing rather than numeric limits. Purpose A is unaffected because WET values are report-only. Purpose B depends on resolving when this conditional monitoring obligation applies. Purpose C depends on the same resolution to classify absent WET results as conditional non-requirement versus missing required evidence.
